plan:
- Microcontroller: ESP32 or Arduino Mega for control logic and communication.
- Actuators: Four high-torque servo motors (e.g., MG996R or digital servos) for each axis, or stepper motors with drivers for higher precision.
- Power System: 5V/10A power supply for servos, separate 5V regulator for MCU if needed, power distribution board.
- Mechanical Frame: Sturdy base plate (e.g., aluminum or acrylic), custom laser-cut or 3D-printed arm links and joint brackets.
- Fasteners & Bearings: M3/M4 screws, nuts, standoffs for assembly; small ball bearings at high-load joints for smooth movement.
- End-Effector: Simple 2-finger gripper actuated by a micro servo, or custom tool mount.

subSteps.title: 3D print all PETG mechanical components
3D print all PLA mounting components
Test fit servos into their respective mounts
Test fit main controller, power supply, and PDB into their mounts
Wire Main Power Supply to Power Distribution Board inputs (5V and GND)
Connect Power Distribution Board to Main Controller for power (5V and GND)
Connect Power Distribution Board to Base, Shoulder, and Elbow Servos for power (5V and GND)
Connect Power Distribution Board to Gripper Actuation Servo for power (5V and GND)
Connect Main Controller PWM pins to Base, Shoulder, Elbow, and Gripper Servos signal pins
Perform continuity check on all power and signal connections
Connect Main Controller to computer via USB
Upload initial firmware to Main Controller to test basic servo control
Apply power to the system and verify all servos respond to basic commands
Verify stable 5V output from Power Distribution Board at all servo connections
Mount base_servo_mount, main_controller_mount, power_supply_mount, and power_distribution_board_mount to the Base Plate using M3 screws and nuts
Mount Main Controller, Power Supply, and Power Distribution Board into their respective mounts
Mount Base Servo into base_servo_mount, then attach Arm Segment 1 (Shoulder Link) with a 608ZZ Ball Bearing for rotation
Mount Shoulder Servo into shoulder_servo_mount, then attach arm_segment_2 (Elbow Link) with a 608ZZ Ball Bearing for rotation. Secure shoulder_servo_mount to Arm Segment 1.
Mount Elbow Servo into elbow_servo_mount, then attach Wrist Plate with a 608ZZ Ball Bearing for rotation. Secure elbow_servo_mount to Arm Segment 2.

Assemble the gripper: Mount Gripper Servo into gripper_servo_mount, attach gripper_body to gripper_servo_mount, and connect gripper_finger_left and gripper_finger_right to gripper_body, driven by the gripper servo. Secure gripper_servo_mount to Wrist Plate.
Route and secure all electrical wires to prevent snagging and ensure proper cable management.
Perform a final system function test to verify all joints and the gripper operate smoothly through their full range of motion.

projectDescription: A four-axis SCARA robot arm, designed for customizable manipulation tasks. It integrates a main controller, base, shoulder, elbow, and gripper actuation servos, a 2-finger gripper, and robust structural components.
